0:2: This is a tiny tale of love in a faraway land.
1:2:
Once upon a time,
there was a kingdom surrounded by a deep, dark forest.
2:2:
The forest was a frightening place, filled with beasts 
and ruled by a powerful witch. Even during the day, the 
forest could be as dark as the winter night. Because of 
this, humans rarely ventured inside.
3:2:
As terrible as the forest was, a beautiful singing voice 
would always pierce the darkness when the moon shone.
4:2:
The voice belonged to a large wolf. She would proudly 
sing toward the moon high atop a cliff every night.
5:2:
The wolf's singing drew in an unforeseen admirer--a 
human prince from the kingdom surrounded by the forest.
6:2:
Every night, the prince would venture into the scary
forest, just to hear the beautiful song.
7:2:
One night, when the wolf finished singing, the prince 
applauded. The voice's identity was hidden because of 
the cliff, but this only piqued the prince's curiosity.
8:2:
The wolf glanced at the prince; wolves are man-eaters, 
after all. “What stupid prey,” she thought. “I should 
eat him now that I'm finished singing.”
9:2:
However, the prince had innocently applauded the wolf, 
who had never before been praised for her singing. She 
hesitated at first, but for some reason, she soon grew 
fond of it and didn't feel like eating him.
10:2:
For several more nights, the wolf sang her song, 
always looking forward to the prince's applause.
11:2:
“But...” the wolf thought.
“If he finds out that I'm a monster, 
he'll get scared and he won't come 
listen to me sing anymore...”
12:2:
So every night, after her song, the wolf would hear the 
prince's applause and retreat into the deep, dark forest.
13:2:
These nights continued, even as the seasons changed... 
On a night like any other, the wolf sang her song toward 
the moon. It was the same, quiet evening for her.
14:2:
However, tonight was a special night for the prince. 
He entered the forest filled with determination.
15:2:
He wanted to see the identity of the 
singing voice with his own two eyes...
The prince climbed the cliff, his heart full.
16:2:
The wolf didn't notice anything unusual at first.
But when she was done singing,
she didn't hear the applause 
that always came afterward.
17:2:
She pondered, and wondered, and glanced down below. 
What?! Why was the prince coming so close to her?!
18:2:
“He'll hate me if he sees me!” The wolf 
panicked. “No one should see what I 
really look like...” She extended a
large paw to cover the prince's eyes.
19:2:
But instead, her claws 
accidentally tore at
the prince's eyes!
20:2:
The wounded prince slipped
from the cliff. The startled wolf thought, 
“If a human falls from this height...” 
and hurriedly seized the prince's arm.
21:2:
At the same time, the terrified prince felt 
the same beastly presence on his arm as the 
one that had just scratched out his eyes, 
which increased his dread tenfold.
22:2:
The prince screamed and struggled, desperate 
to escape the wolf's clutches. The wolf, 
alarmed by his yells, accidentally let 
his arms slip through her grasp.
23:2:
The prince plummeted down the cliff, but then... 
THUMP! He landed safely on some bushes. Though 
he was not harmed from the fall, the wolf's claws 
had injured his eyes...
24:2:
A nearby soldier from the kingdom rushed over 
to the prince. The soldier had heard his screams 
and had come to see the commotion.
25:2:
“The prince must've been hurt by a monster up above!” 
The soldier quickly fired some arrows. The wolf was 
concerned about the prince, but after being barraged by 
arrows, she was forced to escape into the forest.
26:2:
The wounded prince began to gradually lose consciousness. 
The terrible memory of claws in his eyes and the beast's 
grip on his arms became engraved in his mind...
28:2:
The prince, now blind, had brought disappointment and 
shame to the royal family, and his parents locked him 
away in the castle tower.
29:2:
The wolf was concerned about the prince and overheard 
some soldiers in the castle say that he had been locked 
away. “That's awful,” she thought angrily, and she snuck 
into the tower to check on him.
30:2:
The wolf came across a cold room and saw 
the distressed prince sitting inside.
31:2:
The prince sensed someone nearby and raised his face. 
A large cloth was wrapped around his eyes, as if to hide 
something shameful and dirty.
33:2:
“That voice... The singer in the forest?” the prince said.   
“He can recognize me by my voice,” the wolf thought.
34:2:
“Um... Yeah... That's right,” the wolf responded.
“I was attacked by a monster in the forest,” the 
prince said. “But I'm glad that you're alright...”
35:2:
The prince smiled a bit with relief. The wolf felt her 
chest ache when she looked at his ragged figure.
36:2:
“Thank you for coming. But how did you know I was here?” 
The wolf didn't know how to respond to that question...
37:2:
“I-I'm a princess from a nearby kingdom,” the wolf lied, 
remembering that the prince couldn't see her. “I said I 
wanted to visit the ill prince, and they let me in.”
38:2:
“Anyway, forget that. I can't believe
that you're trapped in here!”
39:2:
“But I... I was attacked by a vicious monster and my 
face is awful... My vision is gone... I can't wander 
outside... I'm forbidden from showing my face in public 
ever again...” the prince said, his head hanging sadly.
40:2:
“...Let's ask the witch of the forest to heal your eyes.” 
The prince looked dumbfounded upon hearing her idea.
41:2:
“The witch...? You mean the witch of the forest, 
like the one from the storybook?”
“Storybook? I'm not sure, but the witch can grant all 
wishes. She can fix you!”
42:2:
“The witch lives deep inside the forest. 
I could take you there.”
The wolf was excited at the prospect, but the prince's 
head continued hanging.
43:2:
“It'd be hard to take me deep inside the forest... And 
the monster that rendered me blind... I can still feel 
its claws on me...” The prince couldn't continue, 
his shoulders trembling.
44:2:
The wolf dropped her gaze after hearing his words. She 
looked at her paws; all she saw were sharp claws that 
were made for hurting others.
45:2:
“I want to take the prince from here,” the wolf thought. 
“But I can't hold his hand with these monstrous claws...”
46:2:
Determined, she clasped her paws quietly 
and stepped closer to the prince.
47:2:
“I'll take you to the forest to see the witch.” The 
prince slowly raised his head to the wolf's voice. “But 
just wait here a bit; I'll be back shortly.” She then 
fled the castle tower and ran into the forest.
48:2:
She ran all night through the forest. The sun was rising 
just as she arrived at the witch's house.
49:2:
The witch of the forest turned her gaze to the sudden 
visitor. “Oh! What a rare customer! A man-eating wolf, 
coming all the way here... What's this about?”
50:2:
“I wish to become a human! 
There's someone I want you to see!”
The witch let out a hearty laugh;
sly wolves rarely said such things.
51:2:
“A man-eating wolf, become a human?! How amusing. But 
why on earth... Never mind! No need to divulge the 
details, I believe I already know why.” The wolf growled 
at the witch's mockery.
52:2:
The witch prodded the wolf's nose, the latter looking 
ready to bite at any time. “But of course. I shall 
grant your wish.”
53:2:
“Hmmm... But you do know what I need, yes?”
Strange glowing spheres appeared out of
nowhere. The witch pulled one to her and 
sighed, admiring it.
54:2:
“Beautiful... Each one differs from the 
others, all unique gems.” The sphere's 
vivid glow pulsed in the witch's palm.
55:2:
The witch was a collector with a rather crude temperament. 
In return for granting wishes, she took the requester's 
most cherished possession and turned them into crystals.
56:2:
“The most beautiful hearts are the ones willing to lose 
what's important to them in order to get what they want.”
57:2:
“So, what will your heart reveal to me?” The witch peered 
into the wolf's eyes as if to discern a suitable 
payment. “Hmmm, yes... How about your 
singing voice as compensation?”
58:2:
“M-My singing voice...” The wolf knew that the witch had a 
wicked streak, and she knew she had to sacrifice the most 
important thing to her. Still, her heart 
trembled, doubtful.
59:2:
Her beautiful singing voice that 
the prince praised, or the chance 
to hold his hand...
60:2:
“...Okay. I'll give my singing voice in exchange!”
The mouth of the witch's mask curled up, 
as if giving an evil grin.
62:2:
“I didn't expect to get this from one so prideful, but I 
suppose life is full of surprises. Well, I'm in a good
mood, so I'll give you a little something extra.” 
The witch's eyes twinkled dubiously.
63:2:
“I'll give you whatever form you desire. What do you 
want?” The wolf remembered what she had told the prince.
64:2:
“...I want to look like a princess.”
The witch chuckled softly at the wolf's choice.
66:2:
“But you're sure of that? You and your human friend will 
be devoured by monsters before you even get here.” The 
wolf was unnerved and hung her head, ashamed that the 
witch had seen how futile her plan was.
67:2:
“Didn't think about that, did you? Hmph... Even clever 
wolves can be dull sometimes. I'll modify the spell so 
you can return to wolf form at any time.” A magical light
appeared as she began the ritual.
68:2:
The magical light wrapped around the wolf's body;
a part of the light gathered near the witch.
69:2:
“I've received your singing voice as the toll,” the 
witch said with an eerie smile. The light around 
the wolf suddenly shone bright...and then faded.
70:2:
“...But I'm still a wolf.” The 
wolf looked sad and disappointed.
“It's a complex spell,” the witch said. 
“Give your body one night to get used to it.”
71:2:
Her task complete, the wolf departed the house.
However, the witch stopped her in her tracks.
72:2:
“Ah, I almost forgot. Beware of the moonlight, yes? 
If you fall under it, you will 
immediately turn back into a wolf.”
74:2:
“Soon I'll be human and hold the prince's hand... 
I'm so excited!” Full of hope, the wolf eagerly 
anticipated returning to the castle 
tower where the prince was waiting.
75:2:
After leaving the witch's house, the wolf made 
the journey back to the castle tower. She 
recalled the witch's words about turning into 
a princess. It had already been one night...
76:2:
The prince was in sight. The wolf focused 
on transforming into the princess.
77:2:
The “princess” called out to the prince.
“Prince...”
“Princess? You came back... 
Thank you, but...”
78:2:
“Don't worry! I worked hard to be able to let you out!” 
the princess said brightly, trying to ease the prince.
79:2:
“Alright,” she thought. “I have to get him out of 
the cell. I can destroy the bars as a wolf, but 
the prince needs to get away from them first...”
80:2:
“Hmmm... Ummm... Could you step back a little?”
“O-Oh, okay.” Despite the prince's confusion 
at her instructions, he stepped back from the bars.
81:2:
The princess timidly grasped the prince's tiny, warm 
hand. Though he was scared, he weakly grasped hers back. 
“I gave up my singing voice to be human,” she thought, 
feeling joyful, “but I'm glad I did.”
82:2:
“Let's go to the witch of the forest. 
Make sure you stay close to me, okay?”
83:2:
They entered the deadly forest to travel 
to the witch's house and heal the prince. 
And so, their journey finally began...
84:2:
They talked to each other during their journey. 
She mentioned that she enjoyed running around, 
and he confided that he liked reading.
85:2:
“I love books about flowers,” said the prince. “I can't 
leave the castle that often, so I thought it'd be nice to 
finally see flowers in the outside 
world.” While they were talking...
86:2:
...There was a rustling sound! 
A small monster appeared from the 
bushes and leapt toward the prince!
87:2:
The prince's head barely escaped being bitten by 
the monster. The princess quickly transformed 
into the wolf and brushed the monster away.
88:2:
Everything happened so fast, and for the prince, he 
could not see what was going on. He crouched down on 
the spot, shaking in fear. He couldn't help it; he'd 
recently had a scary experience in the forest.
89:2:
The wolf panicked. “I've gotta do something!”
But she had no idea what to do 
for the frightened prince.
90:2:
She desperately glanced around. A beautiful 
flower field caught her eye. She looked at 
it and remembered what the prince had said. 
“Of course! I can give him flowers!”
91:2:
“Prince, this is for you.”
The princess handed a flower to the prince.
92:2:
“...A flower? It smells so nice...”
“Yeah, you said you love books about flowers.”
The prince smiled happily at the princess's words.
93:2:
“Thank you! I wonder what kind of flower it is. I can't 
see it, though... But I'm more excited to see it once my 
eyes are healed.” She was relieved to see him happier.
94:2:
“I want to thank you...
I know! Do you read a lot of books? 
Wanna hear a story I read one time?”
95:2:
The princess didn't expect the prince to be so happy. 
She felt like she was already becoming closer to him. 
“I'll pick more flowers when I see another 
flower field,” the princess thought, smiling.
96:2:
They walked for what seemed like an eternity 
and didn't notice how dark it had gotten. 
Both of them were exhausted 
from the dangers of the forest.
97:2:
Just as their bellies began to rumble, 
they found a place they could take a rest.
98:2:
“Let's stop here for a bit,” 
said the princess, and she started preparing dinner.
99:2:
“Ta-daaa!”
The princess took out some meat, her favorite food.
“Go on, take a bite!”
100:2:
She then offered the bloody meat to the prince.
“I'm sure the prince will like it too!” 
the princess thought, smiling.
101:2:
“Thank you!” The prince put the meat in his mouth, 
then tilted his head in confusion.
102:2:
“Um... This tastes odd...”
“It's fresh rabbit meat! It's yummy, 
isn't it?” the princess said proudly.
But...
103:2:
“Wait, this is RAW meat...?! Bleurgh!” The prince coughed 
and promptly spat it back out. The princess, who thought 
he would enjoy it, looked at him with a blank expression 
on her face.
104:2:
“S-Sorry. We don't eat raw meat at the castle...” 
The princess felt bad for the prince.
105:2:
“Oh, really...? So how DO you eat meat?”
“Well, we first cook it over the fire. 
We get sick if it's eaten raw.”
106:2:
The princess froze at the word “fire.” 
“Oh, you use...that...?”
She was afraid of it and became tense 
just from thinking about it.
107:2:
“I see... Er, I'll go find some fruit instead.” 
And with that, the princess managed to avoid 
further discussion of fire with the prince.
108:2:
Darkness fell; the witch's house was still 
relatively far away. They began searching 
for a place to spend the night.
109:2:
After wandering for a bit, they found an unstable cabin 
that was covered from top to bottom with mushrooms.
110:2:
“It's pretty rickety... Maybe we could stay for just 
one night...?” the princess said anxiously. 
They firmly held hands and entered the cabin.
111:2:
The inside of the cabin was even darker than the 
forest; only a few blurred shadows were visible. 
The princess squinted her eyes to see what they were.
112:2:
“Whoa... So many corpses...”
The princess realized that the shadows 
were dead goats, lying all over the floor.
114:2:
“Perfect timing. I'm hungry anyway.
Let's eat them for dinner tonight.”
115:2:
“What?!?!” 
The prince, believing that the corpses were humans, was 
taken aback by the princess's outrageous suggestion.
116:2:
The princess left the prince to his own confusion 
and decided to sample one of the goats.
117:2:
Just as the wolf's large fangs were about to sink into 
the goat's stomach, it let out a weak cry.
118:2:
The prince heard the groan and called out to her.
“P-Princess, that human's still alive!”
119:2:
The wolf clicked her tongue and reluctantly stopped eating 
the goat. Nature's law was to eat weak prey, after all.
120:2:
She stared at the prince, disappointed. “So he thinks 
they're human beings,” she thought. “Guess I can't 
do anything about that.”
121:2:
The prince called out to the goats and listened to 
their story. “Princess, these people are starving 
and can't move. Maybe we could help them?”
122:2:
The wolf wanted to be closer to the 
prince, so she grudgingly agreed. 
They set out to find some food 
for the goats.
123:2:
They returned to the cabin with a lot of meat and gave it 
to the goats. “I got a lot!” the princess said proudly. 
“Help yourself!”
124:2:
The prince quickly intervened.
“Princess, wait! We haven't cooked the meat yet!”
Goats are monsters, so they love raw meat, but 
the prince still thought that they were humans.
125:2:
“If I mention how monsters eat raw meat,” the 
princess thought, “he'll know I'm a monster.” 
She decided to play along with his story.
126:2:
“Okay, um...we'd better cook the meat, then. But I've 
never made a fire, so please teach me how to do it.”
She managed to avoid a potentially awkward situation.
127:2:
The princess tried to follow the prince's instructions 
to light the fire, but...
128:2:
“Ahhh! No, I'm scared!” The princess was still 
deathly afraid of fire. She began to cry and 
asked the prince for help.
129:2:
The prince wasn't confident that he could make 
a fire because of his blindness. But he was happy 
that she had asked him for help, so he agreed.
130:2:
“...Okay. I'll give it a shot.”
The prince summoned a little courage for the princess.
131:2:
The meat turned out perfectly! The goats were utterly 
delighted and immediately ate all of it. 
“Cooked meat is amazing, mah!”
132:2:
“Thanks. You helped us, mah. We almost starved to death, 
mah,” one of the goats 
said, thanking the two.
133:2:
“I'm glad! Can we stay here tonight?”
the princess asked.
134:2:
“Of course, mah! It's a little dirty and overrun by 
mushrooms though, mah.” The goats 
took them into their home.
135:2:
The long day finally came to a close.
    The prince was exhausted and dozed off,
but the nocturnal wolf could not sleep.
136:2:
The restless wolf wandered outside the cabin 
and found one of the goats chasing a rabbit.
The rabbit ran swiftly and nimbly, 
and the goat was unable to catch it.
137:2:
“Oh, hi Wolf. Hunting's hard, mah. But you got 
so much meat in the blink of an eye. You're 
pretty good, mah!” the goat said, innocently 
praising the wolf's hunting skills.
138:2:
The wolf shrugged off the compliment. She was worried 
the prince would overhear the goat calling her a wolf. 
When she tried to cut the conversation short...
139:2:
“Oh, that human... Is he emergency rations, mah?”
the goat asked frankly, which startled the wolf.
140:2:
“Not a bad idea. Maybe we should start 
doing that so we won't starve again, mah.
Uh, but if I were you, I'd get a fatter human.
He's so skinny, he'd be a midnight snack, mah.”
141:2:
Normally, the wolf would engage in this banter,
as eating humans was common amongst monsters.  
But now that she was traveling with the prince, 
she became alarmed at the goat's words.
142:2:
“No, no! The prince isn't like that!”
the wolf inadvertently denied. The goat 
didn't let her blunder go unnoticed.
143:2:
“Hmmm? Could it be...? You want to 
get along with humans, mah?!” The 
wolf knew the goat knew the truth, but 
she refused to admit it and kept quiet.
144:2:
“You know it's impossible for monsters and humans to 
get along.” It sounded as if she couldn't be friends 
with the prince. The wolf opened her mouth to speak, 
but no words came out.
145:2:
“You hear of it too, don't you, mah? 
Monsters gobbling up humans, humans 
killing monsters, mah...” The wolf 
hung her head as the goat continued.
146:2:
“No good will come from this, mah. But you did 
save us, so if it's something you really want, 
I'll support you. Good luck, mah.” 
The goat returned to the cabin.
147:2:
The wolf curled up and tried to sleep as the goat's 
words replayed endlessly in her mind. She felt uneasy; 
up until then, she'd been happy to hold the prince's 
hand as the princess, believing there was 
nothing to fear.
148:2:
But her true form was a monster that the prince 
hated. And he still didn't know that she was the 
one who had blinded him. If he EVER found out...
149:2:
“It'll be okay,” the wolf told herself. 
“If I can just keep this up a bit longer...”
She didn't sleep that night.
151:2:
The princess and the prince left the cabin. The goats 
thanked them again and prayed for their safe travels.
152:2:
“Good luck, mah. Don't eat him by accident!”
said the goat the wolf had talked to 
the night before. The prince didn't 
understand, but she did.
153:2:
“I won't eat him...” the princess thought.
Needing to calm her anxious heart, she 
pulled the prince's hand and set off again.
154:2: At dusk, they found a lake in the middle of the forest.
155:2:
The scarlet sunset's reflection danced brilliantly 
on the lake's surface. The area appeared safe, so 
they decided to stay there for the night.
156:2:
After dinner, they spent some more time talking.
“Prince, you read a lot of books, don't you?”
“Yeah, like books with games you can play with others.”
“Oh, really? What's that like?” the princess asked, 
curious. She was used to playing alone.
157:2:
The prince was delighted that she was interested, 
so he happily explained one of the game's rules.
158:2:
“...So there's a winner and a loser... Okay! 
Let's play!” the princess said eagerly.
159:2:
“Oh, and let's make it so that the loser has to 
grant the winner's wish,” the prince added.
“Alright! I'm not gonna lose!” said the princess 
haughtily, feeling like she'd already won.
160:2:
“...I lost.”
The princess clenched her teeth, 
blinking back tears.
161:2:
“You know a lot of words that I don't...”
“Eheheh... I read a lot of books,” 
the prince said, sheepishly grinning.
162:2:
“Um... Since I won, can I tell you my wish?”
“Oh... Y-Yeah...” The princess was still upset 
at losing, but she regained her composure and 
waited for the prince to speak.
163:2:
“Princess, I-I want to hear you sing,”
the prince said shyly.
164:2:
“What...? Sing...?” Her singing voice, which the prince 
had come to hear every night, had been given to the witch 
in exchange for turning into a princess. She hadn't sung 
once since they'd started traveling together.
165:2:
It was hard to imagine what her 
singing voice was like now.
166:2:
“I love your singing voice...”
“Ummm...” 
The princess thought long and hard. “If I don't sing, 
will he no longer trust me...?” She felt pressured.
167:2:
“...Okay, I'll do it.” The princess nervously cleared her 
throat, opened her mouth, and started singing.
168:2:
But her voice was nothing like her old one. In fact, 
it was horrible! The prince looked blank; she sounded 
completely different from what he remembered.
169:2:
The princess started coughing, embarrassed. 
“Sorry! I guess I'm exhausted from all this 
traveling... I'll sing again after I've rested...”
170:2:
“Oh no! I'm sorry I forced you to sing...
We should sleep early so you can rest.”
The prince's gentle words cut into the princess, 
who felt guilty for lying about her voice.
171:2:
Dawn arrived. The prince was in a deep slumber,
but the wolf remained unable to sleep.
172:2:
She slowly walked around the lake,
her head buzzing with anxiety.
173:2:
“It's impossible for monsters and humans to get along...”
The goat's words replayed endlessly in her mind.
“I need to stay in princess form,” the wolf thought.
“I can't be with the prince unless I keep lying...”
174:2:
She felt conflicted about her feelings for the prince 
and her constant lies. The wolf prodded the lake's 
surface, as if to erase her uneasiness.
175:2:
The water slowly rippled. The wolf glanced at it and 
saw her monstrous reflection. She heaved a big sigh 
and prodded the lake's surface again.
176:2:
The princess hesitated, lost in thought. 
She was holding a flower she 
had picked for the prince.
177:2:
Eventually, the princess nodded with 
resolve and transformed gently to avoid 
crushing the flower.
178:2:
She was attempting to give the flower to the prince 
in her true form. Her fingers trembled with anxiety.
179:2:
...But in the end, she never gave him
the flower as the wolf.
180:2:
The flower seemed to be telling her that 
her beastly self would never be good enough 
for him, and that she would always be a monster 
who only knew how to hurt others.
181:2:
“...Princess? What's wrong?”
The wolf was startled to hear the prince's voice.
She sighed sadly and transformed back into the princess.
182:2:
“...No, it's nothing. Here you go.”
The princess wistfully smiled as 
she gave the flower to the prince.
183:2:
The prince's usual happy smile 
filled her with pain that day.
184:2:
The princess led the prince through a dark cave. 
Despite her best efforts to carefully guide him, 
the ground that he was standing on collapsed!
185:2:
“PRINCE!” 
The princess seized his hand, but she 
could not lift him up in her current form.
186:2:
She could rescue him easily in wolf form... But if her 
hand, still holding his, turned into the wolf's, he'd 
know she was a monster. She desperately tried to pull 
him up, her entire body shaking.
187:2:
Unfortunately, she couldn't do it any longer.
She ran out of energy and unwillingly let go of his hand.
189:2:
“OH NO!” shouted the princess. She looked where he had 
fallen and saw him lying in a small, shallow hole.
190:2:
Her mind went blank and her heart filled with dread. But 
the prince soon sat up and waved. He was perfectly fine!
191:2:
The ground that had given way was hollow, so the prince 
didn't suffer any injuries. The princess felt relieved.
192:2:
But... The princess looked at her hand, 
a feeble and tiny hand that couldn't help the 
prince. She began to feel uneasy about keeping 
him safe in the future.
193:2:
While traversing through the cave, they came 
across a strange area filled with many holes, 
which looked like gaping mouths 
in the darkness.
194:2:
“There might be something dangerous in them!” 
the princess thought. To protect the prince, 
she stood in front of one of the holes 
and peered inside it.
196:2:
Tons of small black creatures emerged 
from the holes! The princess and the 
prince soon found themselves 
completely surrounded.
197:2:
The prince, sensing the princess's alarm, 
seized her hand and braced himself. 
“Don't move,” the princess said, 
ready to fend off the creatures.
198:2:
But the creatures only twitched their nostrils in 
curiosity. “Hmmm... Maybe they're not harmful?” the 
princess said. Just as she turned her back...
199:2:
...The creature next to the prince 
opened its mouth wide!
200:2:
“DON'T EAT HIM!”

creature and pushed it backward, 
sending it flying into a rock wall.

The creature, now with a lump 
on its head, started to cry.

“Flower...smells good...and tasty...”

The prince tried approaching the crying creature.
“No, Prince! It's too dangerous. Let me do it,” 
the princess offered, not wanting him to know 
that the creatures were monsters.

The creatures quietly told her that they were 
moles who lacked sight, but had an excellent 
sense of smell and loved flowers.
205:2:
“Flowers don't bloom in the cave,” they said, “but 
sometimes the wind carries in flower petals.”
206:2:
“Flowers are our favorite, but since they're 
so scarce, we fight over them when they come

Hiding that the creatures were moles, the 
princess relayed their story to the prince.
208:2:
“Oh... I want to share my flower, but it's too 
important to me... I'm sorry.” The moles became 
sad and made high pitiful squeals with their noses.
209:2:
“Princess...why don't we get flowers for them?”
the prince suggested.
210:2:
The princess agreed. 
“Yeah, let's do it! Let's go look for flowers.”
211:2:
The moles stopped crying and became happy.
Following the petals riding on the wind,
the two set off to find another flower field.

The princess gasped upon arriving at the flower field.
Flowers of every color were blooming, made even more 
radiant by the setting sun. It was the most beautiful 
sight she had ever laid eyes on.
213:2:
“It smells wonderful, doesn't it, Princess?”
“Yeah... I've never seen such a pretty field before.”
“Really? Oh, I wish I could see it...”
214:2:
The princess closed her eyes for a moment and took it
all in, wishing she could show this to the prince.
“Okay, let's pick some flowers!”
215:2: They gathered a lot of flowers and went back to the cave.
216:2:
The moles were ecstatic at the flowers 
the princess and the prince had brought, 
and they began to jump and run around
the pair, clamoring for the flowers.
217:2:
“Okay, I'm handing them out now!”
The princess gave a flower to each mole one at a time.
But one mole was anxious and couldn't wait any longer...
218:2:
CHOMP!
The mole sank its teeth into the flowers the princess

didn't care and started chewing on the flowers.
“Om nom nom! They're sooo yummy!”
219:2:
The moles who had already received their flowers

220:2:
The prince was off to the side, telling one of the moles

221:2:
“Thank you so much,” said the mole. “Why don't

out some food for the princess and the prince,

223:2:
They returned to the flower field. 
The princess wanted to give a 
special flower to the prince.
224:2:
The lantern the prince held illuminated 
the field; the moonlight could occasionally 
be seen peeking from behind the clouds.
225:2:
As the princess gave the best flower 
to the prince, she took his hand, 
and he shyly squeezed hers in return.
226:2:
The princess felt warmth from the prince's hand 
and immediately forgot all of her troubles. 
She wished to keep things like this forever.
227:2: For a moment, the princess completely let her guard down.
228:2: The moonlight appeared from the clouds and shone on them.
229:2:
It shone on them briefly, but that was all that was 
needed for the princess's hand, still holding the 
prince's, to change into the wolf's. A shivering 
feeling coursed through the prince's hand.
230:2:
It was the feeling of a monster that had 
both slashed the prince's eyes and 
gripped his arms. He tried not to 
cry out in fear.
231:2:
But...why?
Why had her hand changed into the monster's...?
232:2:
The prince couldn't believe it.
Could she be...?!
233:2:
The princess... She's the monster...?!
He scrambled away from her.
234:2:
“Wait, Prince... It's not...”
She tried to explain, but her 
words fell on deaf ears.
235:2:
“No... Don't come any closer...”
The prince moved further away, 
not knowing that he was near 
the edge of a cliff.
236:2:
“Prince, watch out!” The princess leapt at him just before 
he fell and seized his hand. The lantern he was holding 
slid out of his grasp and tumbled down the cliff.
237:2:
“Prince, give me your other hand, or you'll fall!”
The prince hung his head and didn't move.
238:2:
“Princess, did you lie to me...?”
“What are you talking about...? 
Hang on... I'll pull you up!”
But she was too weak to lift him to safety.
240:2:
“N-No, it's just your imagination! Maybe you 
got confused when I gave you that flower?”
241:2:
The princess still felt guilty about lying to him, 
but she couldn't risk him knowing that she was 
really the monster that had blinded him...
242:2:
“Please. Take my hand...” She desperately tried to 
grab at the prince's other hand, but he did nothing 
and continued to hang his head.
243:2:
Misfortune then struck. The clouds hiding the moon 
vanished, bathing the two in pure moonlight.
244:2:
The spell was broken on the princess, and she fully 
reverted to the wolf. She had no excuse now.
245:2:
“No... This is... No... It's not...”
The prince felt a beastly paw holding his hand. 
His suspicions were confirmed.
247:2:
“...”
The wolf couldn't think of anything to defend herself.
250:2: “Let go of my hand, you monster!”
251:2:
The wolf's eyes welled up with tears; 
his words had cut deeply into her. 
She could barely breathe. Nothing had 
ever caused her heart so much pain before.
252:2:
The wolf inadvertently loosened her grip, 
and the prince swung his hand free.
253:2:
All she could do was stare at him 
falling down the cliff.
254:2:
The wolf kept staring at the spot where he had fallen, 
her mind completely blank.
255:2:
...After what seemed like an eternity,
a red light shone in the dark forest.
256:2:
Soon, the forest turned crimson. The fire from 
the fallen lantern was burning the forest!
257:2:
The wolf snapped out of her reverie when she heard trees 
burning. “The prince is in danger! I've gotta help him!”
258:2:
Flames engulfed more trees and rapidly spread. 
The wolf instinctively wanted to run away.
259:2:
Her body trembled; she hated fire more than anything. 
But if the prince died in this blazing inferno...
260:2:
“PRINCE------!!!” Summoning all her courage, 
the wolf leapt into the burning forest.
261:2:
After desperately searching the burning forest,
the wolf finally found the prince.
262:2:
Surrounded by fiery trees,
he fearfully cried out for help.
263:2: The wolf carefully approached the prince.
264:2:
“Prince... I came to help you...”
she said softly.
265:2:
“Princess...”

who had destroyed his eyes, yet she had overcome 
her fear of fire to save his life...
266:2:
Neither of them said anything. 
They could only stand near each other 
as the forest burned around them.
267:2:
Soon, they heard a ferocious roar from far away. 
The burning trees fell and shook the entire forest.
They looked at where the roar had come from.
268:2:
It had come from a great monster that towered over 
the trees. It roared again, its roar filled with 
the utmost fury. Neither the wolf nor the prince 
had heard such a frightening monster before.
270:2:
Items from the witch's collection were among
them, shouting in panicked voices.
271:2:
“The witch of the forest is furious!” one of 
the creatures yelled. “Her collection was 
destroyed and she's on a rampage, just like

272:2:
The wolf and the prince turned to each other. 
“The witch of the forest...?” the wolf pondered.
“It's my fault her things are gone,” the prince said.
273:2:
“Hmmm... How can I defeat her?” 
the wolf thought. It wouldn't be easy 
to triumph over such a terrible monster.

275:2:
“Princess, let's apologize to the witch.”
The wolf was startled at his suggestion.
276:2:
“Apologize...?”
“If you do bad things, you have to apologize.”
277:2:
“If you do bad things, you have 
to apologize...” the wolf repeated.
“Come on!” said the prince. “...Um, Princess?”

The wolf hesitated, then nodded.
“...Right. Let's go!”

They had finally arrived at the witch's house...or

It was now an unrecognizable pile of rubble.
280:2:
They spotted the angry witch further ahead,

281:2:
“What do we do?” the princess asked nervously. 
“I don't think she's gonna listen to us...”
282:2:
“It'll be okay,” the prince assured her.
“What do you mean?” The princess looked at him.

“Princess, you're very strong.”
“Uh... Prince...?”

he joking or being serious? She 
started feeling a little panicked.

A livid roar and the shaking ground halted their

285:2:
“She's getting closer to us...!” The princess tried to

“Wait! The witch might listen to us once

287:2:
“How do we do that?”

“Wait... What?!”
This sounded easier said than done.
The prince tried to coax her.
288:2:
“Please, just try to knock her out!”
“Um... A-Alright... I'll give it a shot!”
The princess transformed into the wolf

They managed to calm the witch down and return her 
to normal. The smoke from the battle cleared away.

The witch appeared to have fainted, but she soon awoke

291:2:
“No... You destroyed my most precious item...

You don't understand,” the witch sputtered,

292:2:
She gestured her hand toward them. Magical power

Just before that power was unleashed on the two...

“...Well now! Have you become more honest?

296:2:
For some reason, there was no malice in her voice,

“At any rate, you have something for me, don't you?”
The princess nodded, remembering why

“Yes... Please, Witch!

The witch's face distorted, her expression

“Hmmm... But you burned the forest and my collection.

The witch chuckled. “No, no, I won't take his life.

“Let's see... I'll deprive you of all memories with the

“Normally, I wouldn't take this much for healing

“Well? What do you think? You've been

Finally, she braced herself, determined.

“NO! I won't let you!”

The princess seized the prince's hand. “It's okay.

“Prince, I'm sorry. For everything that I've done.”
The prince tried to respond, but...

“Payment accepted!”
The witch interrupted them and began the ritual.

The princess was caught in the magical light,

328:2:
Once upon a time,
there was a kingdom surrounded by a deep, dark forest.
329:2:
The forest was a frightening place, filled with beasts 
and ruled by a powerful witch. Even during the day, the 
forest could be as dark as the winter night. Because of 
this, humans rarely ventured inside.
330:2:
As terrible as the forest was, a singing voice 
would always pierce the darkness when the moon shone.
331:2:
...Well, it wasn't very good singing. 
The voice belonged to a large wolf, 
who would sit high atop a cliff every 
night and sing toward the moon.
332:2:
“...Why am I singing...?
I'm terrible at this...”
For some reason, whenever the wolf felt 
sad, she'd come to this cliff and sing.
333:2:
She tried to remember why, 
but her memories were very hazy.
334:2:
“My heart feels empty...”
The wolf's lonely song faded away
into the darkness of the night.
When she finished, silence fell.
335:2:
The wolf stared into the night sky, as still as a statue.
Suddenly, she heard a noise from nearby.
336:2:
“Ooof... Mmmph...” A strange human climbed 
the cliff and stood right in front of her. 
The wolf was surprised.
337:2:
Humans and wolves were mortal enemies. And the small human 
before her looked especially tender and soft.
338:2:
The wolf hadn't been particularly craving humans, but 
a midnight snack had just presented itself to her. 
She raised a large paw, ready to 
kill the human and eat him.
339:2:
Just before she struck him, however, 
he caught her off guard and held out something.
340:2:
The wolf was suddenly overwhelmed by colors of every 
shade imaginable. For some reason, she was filled with 
nostalgia and a gentle, familiar scent.
341:2:
“...Flowers...?”
The human was holding a small bouquet.
342:2:
“Yes, it's for you,”
the human said, smiling.
The wolf looked puzzled.
343:2: “I came to see you again, Princess.”
344:2:
Suddenly, she was overcome with emotion. Tears 
welled up in her eyes and flowed down her face. 
Sadness and anguish burst from her heart.
345:2:
She didn't understand what he had said to her, 
but she felt her lonely, empty heart being filled.
346:2:
The wolf lowered her paw and reached for 
the bouquet. She gently held the tiny 
flowers, which trembled ever so slightly, 
and sat down on the spot.
347:2:
The human smiled and sat down next to the wolf. Her 
blurred vision made his smile seem to quiver.
348:2:
They cuddled under the moonlight as 
the wolf sang again. It wasn't very 
good singing, but the human listened 
to it joyfully nonetheless.
349:2:
After that night, the wolf sang not toward the 
moon, but for the human sitting next to her.
350:2:
And although the singing was not great,
it was filled with warmth and honesty, 
and it brightened the dark forest, forever and ever.
